context_edits.purpose: add NumberUtils.offsetToFloorMultiple (D): the offset from a value to the largest multiple of a step at or below it (multiple minus value, zero or negative)
add DateUtils.wholeHours (A: whole hours from a duration and its offset to the hour start) and DateUtils.minutesPastHour (P2: minutes past the hour, negating the same offset)
add FastDatePrinter.appendZoneOffset (C): the +/-HHMM / +/-HH:MM writer, which calls D, then A for the hours and P2 for the minutes
TimeZoneNumberRule.appendTo (patterns Z and ZZ) delegates to appendZoneOffset; output identical (hours = offset/1h, minutes = offset/1min - 60*hours)

decoys.decl: final Date date, final String pattern, final TimeZone timeZone)

ownership_reason: NumberUtils.offsetToFloorMultiple (D) returns multiple - value: the offset from the value to the largest multiple of the step at or below it. Its javadoc fixes that orientation (zero or negative, value + offset is the multiple, 330 with step 60 gives -30) and its code matches. The new, passing NumberUtilsTest.testOffsetDownToStep pins D directly. DateUtils.minutesPastHour (P2) is a second production caller of D that runs under the trigger; it negates D's value to get the minutes past the hour, and the new, passing DateUtilsTest.testMinutesIntoTheHour pins it (5h30 gives 30, 12h45m59s gives 45), so D's convention is the documented one. FastDatePrinter.appendZoneOffset (C) takes the magnitude of the zone offset, supplies (offset, MILLIS_PER_HOUR) to D in the documented order, passes D's value unchanged to DateUtils.wholeHours (A) for the hour digits and takes the minute digits from P2; its sign, digits and colon match its javadoc. A's javadoc says it returns the number of whole hours, rounding down, never up (the hour that starts at or before millis), and that offsetToHour is D's zero-or-negative value, so millis + offsetToHour is the start of the hour. The variant computes (millis - offsetToHour) / MILLIS_PER_HOUR, which lands on the following hour for any duration that is not a whole number of hours: for Asia/Kolkata (+05:30) it returns 6, and the entry point DateFormatUtils.format(Date, String, TimeZone) prints +06:30 instead of +05:30 for pattern ZZ. Whole-hour zones give an offset of 0, so the existing suite (New York, GMT-3, CET, UTC, default America/Los_Angeles) cannot see the difference. Restoring the + in A alone makes the trigger and the full suite pass. Flipping D, or negating or swapping the definer arguments in C, makes A reject the offset with an IllegalArgumentException, and flipping D also breaks both ownership tests, so no decoy edit absorbs the fault.

compensating.why: one-line definer edit: offsetToFloorMultiple returns the non-negative remainder (value minus the multiple) instead of the documented offset from the value to the multiple
one-line caller edit: appendZoneOffset negates the definer's value before passing it to wholeHours
one-line caller edit: appendZoneOffset swaps the two arguments it supplies to the definer
